decisive_items: Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10
weakness and numbness in both legs and difficulty with urination
Positron emission tomography–computed tomography showed osteolytic destruction of the neural arch of T9
response.rationale: The defining presentation is a posterior epidural abscess causing spinal cord compression with bilateral leg weakness and urinary difficulty; the MRI finding directly establishes the diagnosis. Adjacent vertebral/lamina destruction reflects an associated osteomyelitis, but the acute neurologic syndrome is best explained by the epidural abscess.

rejected.why: Osteomyelitis is present on imaging but is secondary/adjacent to the epidural abscess and does not best explain the acute cord compression symptoms.
Discitis is not supported because MRI identifies a posterior epidural abscess and T9 lamina lesion without evidence of primary intervertebral disc involvement.
